No new ideas today: two short problems on Lectures 6 and 7, with one new
button of Excel. Do each one alone, then open "Check your result". Every
question on this page has its answer: try first, then check.

## Recall

- **Lecture 6:** SUM, AVERAGE and MAX work on a range, for example
  `=MAX(E2:E25)`.
- **Lecture 7:** a filter shows only some rows; a chart shows the answer
  to one question.
- **AI help:** an AI summary sounds sure, but its numbers can be wrong.
  Check every number with the data (Lectures 2 and 9).

![A PivotTable: the total of each type.](images/pivot.png){width=100%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="=SUM(E2)|a theme"}
Which formula gives the biggest sale in E2:E25?
:   =MAX(E2:E25)

    Why: MAX gives the highest value of a range.

You want to see only the rows of the type Paper. What do you use?
:   a filter

    Why: A filter shows only the rows that you choose.

An AI summary gives a number. What do you do before you use it?
:   check it with the data

    Why: AI can write wrong numbers in a sure voice.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Rana's month in a PivotTable

Rana has the 24 sales of the Sunrise shop in March: the week, the item,
the type (Paper, Drinks, Bags), the quantity and the total in JD. A
**PivotTable** sums them by type or by week in a few clicks: **Insert ›
PivotTable**, a field in **Rows**, the Total in **Values**.

{{< sim file="sims/pivot-lab.html" poster="sims/pivot-lab.png" title="Pivot Lab: summarize Rana's month" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · By type and by week · 15 min"}
1. In **Pivot Lab**, choose Rows **Type** and Values **Sum of Total**.
   Which type sold the most?
2. Change the rows to **Week**. Which week was the best, and which the
   weakest?
3. Choose Rows **Type** and Values **Average of Total**. Which type has the
   biggest average sale?

*Your product:* three short answers, each with its number.

::: {.check}
1. Paper sold the most: 206 JD (Drinks 71, Bags 78; 355 JD in all).
2. The third week was the best (112 JD); the second was the weakest
   (63 JD).
3. Paper has the biggest average sale: about 20.6 JD.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The PivotTable"}
Use Pivot Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Bags, 78 JD|the first week"}
Rows Type, Values Sum of Total: which type sold the most?
:   Paper, 206 JD

    Why: Paper has the biggest sum of the three types.

Rows Week, Values Sum of Total: which week was the weakest?
:   the second week, 63 JD

    Why: 63 JD is the smallest of the four weeks.

You add new sales to the data. What must you do to the PivotTable?
:   Refresh it

    Why: A PivotTable does not update by itself.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Is the AI summary right?

Rana asked an AI tool for a short summary of March for the staff
newsletter. Before she uses it, she checks every sentence with the facts
of her PivotTable.

![An AI summary, checked.](images/ai-summary.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/summary-check.html" poster="sims/summary-check.png" title="Summary Check: is the AI right?" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Check the summary · 12 min"}
1. In **Summary Check**, mark each of the six sentences true or wrong.
   Use the PivotTable facts at the top.
2. Write a corrected summary of three true sentences, each with a number.

*Your product:* six marks and a summary of three true sentences.

::: {.check}
True: the total of 355 JD; the third week was the best (112 JD); the
average sale was about 15 JD. Wrong: "Bags sold the most" (Paper, 206
JD); "sales grew every week" (the second week fell to 63 JD); "the
biggest sale was a bag for 48 JD" (notebooks, 60 JD). A good summary:
"March sales were 355 JD. Paper sold the most, 206 JD. The best week was
the third, with 112 JD."
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The AI summary"}
Use Summary Check. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Bags sold the most|yes, every week"}
The AI says "Bags sold the most". The PivotTable says Bags 78 JD and Paper 206 JD. What is true?
:   Paper sold the most

    Why: 206 JD is more than 78 JD; the AI was wrong.

The weeks were 87, 63, 112 and 93 JD. Did sales grow every week?
:   no, the second week fell

    Why: 63 JD is less than 87 JD.

What do you add under an AI summary that you checked?
:   a short AI-use statement

    Why: It says honestly that AI helped and that you checked it.
:::
:::

## Wrap-up {.summary}

- You can summarize a list by type or by week with a PivotTable.
- You can check an AI summary of data number by number, and correct it.
